quotes.speaker: Taylor Jenkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Taylor Jenkins on the importance of building team chemistry early
quotes.excerpt: I definitely reserve the right to change my mind day-to-day, especially this early, such a new group.
quotes.quote: I definitely reserve the right to change my mind day-to-day, especially this early, such a new group, new systems. Obviously you want to find the chemistry and see how guys, whether it's body language, how they play off each other, the reads. It's not just guards in the backcourt, it's also with our bigs. The way I look at it is obviously you want to start the game strong, play in the middle of the game strong, you want to finish strong. I've been very big on how we blend our bench and rely on that and how we have chemistry with different advantage creators offensively, or do we have our point of attack defense and our rim anchors out there as well.
quotes.social_post: Taylor Jenkins says he reserves the right to change his mind on lineups and rotations early in the season as he looks to find chemistry with a new group and new systems.

quotes.speaker: Taylor Jenkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Taylor Jenkins on rookie development and defensive expectations
quotes.excerpt: They know they're going to be held very high to a standard on the defensive side.
quotes.quote: I think their habits, that's the biggest thing, has been great. Everything we're asking of them, like all of these guys, we haven't really gotten to a lot of the individualized player development yet. It's been heavy practice these last three days. Their habits have been great, how they show up, they put great work in in the training room, in the weight room, and then on the court. They're attacking every opportunity they get. I've been really impressed from what I saw in Summer League. Those guys showed well, but now they're going up against guys that have played in the league for a number of years and a different level of physicality and speed. When they get their opportunities, I think they're playing at a very high competitive level and they have a lot of growth opportunities as well. Luckily, when it comes to those guys, they know they're going to be held very high to a standard on the defensive side.
quotes.social_post: Taylor Jenkins has been impressed with the habits of his rookies during training camp but notes they are being held to a very high standard on the defensive side.

quotes.speaker: Taylor Jenkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Taylor Jenkins on improving team communication and defensive intensity
quotes.excerpt: It becomes infectious the rest of the play and then that translates to a little rhythm.
quotes.quote: I'd say just level of communication is slowly getting a little bit better, learning our terminology, learn the cadence of communication. It's been something I've been really focusing on. It's like a chain reaction, start of a possession to the end of the possession. We're trying to train at a very high velocity and speed. It's constant chaos in the half court and the full court. The shot clock's low, guys have to process the advantage that's there on offense, or then how we're going to start our defense and pressure as much as we can and not just rely on a 24-second shot clock and have rest time built in. So we're trying to stress the mind just as much as we are physically. I identified why, and it started with our defensive intensity, making sure we're starting every play 94 feet. It becomes infectious the rest of the play and then that translates to a little rhythm on the offensive side when we start hitting that lull.
quotes.social_post: Taylor Jenkins is emphasizing defensive intensity and communication starting 94 feet away to help the team avoid lulls and maintain rhythm on the offensive side.

quotes.speaker: Taylor Jenkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Taylor Jenkins on the mental challenges of implementing new systems
quotes.excerpt: I think the mental is the one thing we're trying to stress a lot.
quotes.quote: I think the mental is the one thing we're trying to stress a lot and naturally the physical is allowing us to do that. We're constantly keeping practice moving, we're changing things up, we're changing the rules of the game. I'm getting on them when they don't follow the rules and they're struggling because then it impacts the other four guys. If it's two guys, we need all five guys, we need the guys on the sideline to be on the same page. So I think the mental is the one thing we're trying to stress a lot and naturally the physical is allowing us to do that.
quotes.social_post: Taylor Jenkins says the coaching staff is using physical drills to stress the mental side of the game, forcing players to follow rules and stay on the same page.

quotes.speaker: Taylor Jenkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Taylor Jenkins on teaching intent and purpose during practice
quotes.excerpt: We want to give them what is the intent and what is the why.
quotes.quote: When we set something up, we want to give them what is the intent and what is the why. Why are we putting this rule on here? Why are we putting you at a disadvantage here? What are we trying to account for? And bring it all the way back, what's our recipe for success offensively and defensively? We want to get this type of result, this type of shot. We want to prevent this type of shot. So whatever the atmosphere is, and whatever we're creating for you guys, you're going to be able to problem solve quickly.
quotes.social_post: Taylor Jenkins explains his coaching philosophy of teaching intent and purpose so players can problem solve quickly during games.

quotes.speaker: Taylor Jenkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Taylor Jenkins on the importance of defensive identity and accountability
quotes.excerpt: We want to be all out, aggressive for 48, attack mentality.
quotes.quote: I'm not one to necessarily single out a lot of individual guys. I think our guards are doing a great job when we talk about how we offensive rebound and we try to, again, I'm going to hold them to this, can we do this for 48 minutes, for 82 games? I know there's challenges, distractions, there's excuses, we don't want to be built that way. But I think our guards are doing a great job. We try to highlight the times that we're doing and highlight the times that we're not and it's pretty glaring, because we want to be all out, aggressive for 48, attack mentality. Same thing with our anchors, our bigs doing a great job whether it's the pick and roll coverages or protecting the paint because that's a huge priority of ours.
quotes.social_post: Taylor Jenkins says he wants his team to maintain an aggressive attack mentality for 48 minutes and 82 games, noting that the team does not want to be built on excuses.

quotes.speaker: Taylor Jenkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Taylor Jenkins on the 365 development model and G League integration
quotes.excerpt: It's a 365 model. It's our off-season program, but obviously in-season, how we develop guys.
quotes.quote: There was a lot of intentionality to hiring one coach at a time for my coaching staff. And then when it got to the point to start focusing on the Herd and having them be an extension of our staff, that's the way I view it, it's a 365 model. It's our off-season program, but obviously in-season, how we develop guys, whether it's on assignment or they're transferred. I'm a product of the minor leagues. So I understand if you truly care and have a purpose behind how you treat the G League experience, it's not a demotion, it's not a punishment, it's a development opportunity. You're not going down, you're going to. So that's hopefully something that's shared throughout the entire organization.
quotes.social_post: Taylor Jenkins emphasizes his 365 development model, stating that G League assignments are a development opportunity rather than a punishment for players.
